findings.claim: The glossary defines individual liberty as respect for and tolerance of other people’s rights, choices and beliefs.
findings.truth: Individual liberty concerns personal freedoms, such as speech and movement, within limits set by law; the lesson’s content defines it correctly.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.1; internal consistency with L01 content_html

findings.claim: around 18% of the population described themselves as belonging to an ethnic group other than White British
findings.truth: In the 2021 Census for England and Wales, 74.4% identified as White: English, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish or British, so 25.6% identified otherwise.
findings.evidence: ONS, Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.truth: The 1801 union created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. Northern Ireland was created by the partition settlement in 1920–21.
findings.evidence: UK Parliament, An Act for the Union of Great Britain and Ireland; House of Commons Library, Parliament and Northern Ireland, 1921–2021 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Following the UK’s departure from the EU in January 2020, freedom of movement between the UK and EU member states ended.
findings.truth: The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, but free movement ended on 31 December 2020 and the points-based system began on 1 January 2021.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, The UK’s points-based immigration system: information for EU citizens (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Applying for asylum is a legal right under international law, established by the 1951 UN Refugee Convention.
findings.truth: Article 14 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights recognises the right to seek and enjoy asylum. The 1951 Convention defines refugee status and provides protections, but does not expressly establish a right of asylum. Recommend a coordinated change to all repeated content, question and answer-key references rather than partial edits.
findings.evidence: UNHCR, Note on International Protection; UNHCR, Note on Asylum (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: member states are expected to spend at least 2% of GDP on defence
findings.truth: At the 2025 Hague Summit, NATO allies committed to invest 5% of GDP annually in core defence and defence- and security-related spending by 2035.
findings.evidence: NATO, The Hague Summit Declaration (2025); NATO, Defence investment and NATO’s 5% commitment (updated 2026) (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: When the UK left the EU in January 2020 it left the EU’s institutions (the European Parliament, the European Court of Justice, the single market, the customs union).
findings.truth: The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, but remained in the single market and customs union during the transition period until 31 December 2020.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Public funds: transition period guidance (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: The police may stop and search only when they have reasonable grounds to suspect someone of carrying weapons, stolen goods or items for use in crime.
findings.truth: Reasonable grounds are usually required, but a senior officer can authorise suspicionless searches in limited circumstances, including under section 60 powers.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Police powers to stop and search: your rights; PACE Code A 2023 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: aged 18–70 who are registered to vote
findings.truth: In England and Wales, eligible jurors are aged 18 to 75 when their jury service begins.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Jury service: Who can be on a jury (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: custodial sentences of up to six months for a single offence
findings.truth: A magistrates’ court can impose up to six months for a summary offence and up to twelve months for an either-way offence.

findings.claim: At age 16, a person in England, Wales and Northern Ireland may ... marry with parental consent
findings.truth: Since 27 February 2023, the minimum age of marriage in England and Wales is 18, even with parental consent. Scotland permits marriage at 16; Northern Ireland permits it at 16 with the required consent.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Legal age of marriage in England and Wales rises to 18; Scottish Government marriage consultation; nidirect marriage guidance (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Westminster retains control over reserved areas including criminal justice policy in many instances.
findings.truth: Policing and justice are transferred matters on which the Northern Ireland Assembly can legislate. Westminster retains control of reserved and excepted matters, including immigration and national security.

findings.claim: around half of adults released from custody go on to commit further offences within one year
findings.truth: For the April–June 2024 cohort, 67.1% of adults released after custodial sentences under 12 months committed a proven reoffence within a year; rates vary substantially by sentence length.
findings.evidence: Ministry of Justice, Proven reoffending statistics: April to June 2024 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: the Geneva Conventions include ... the ban on using certain weapons such as chemical weapons and landmines
findings.truth: The Geneva Conventions and wider humanitarian law protect people in conflict. Chemical weapons and anti-personnel landmines are prohibited by separate weapons treaties.
findings.evidence: ICRC, International law on the conduct of hostilities: overview; ICRC, Weapons and disarmament (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: To become a magistrate, a person must apply to the Judicial Appointments Commission
findings.truth: The Judicial Appointments Commission does not recruit magistrates. Local Advisory Committees on Justices of the Peace assess candidates and recommend appointments.
findings.evidence: Judicial Appointments Commission, What we do; GOV.UK, Advisory Committees on Justices of the Peace (fetched 2026-09-04)

summary: Checked all 13 lessons against the assessment and subject-content sections of the specification and fetched official sources. Fourteen findings have surgical edits; one repeated asylum-law attribution needs a coordinated editorial decision.
